title: Chamberlain at Little Round Top
text:
On July 2, 1863, the second day of the Battle of Gettysburg, the 20th Maine Infantry, about 385 men under Colonel Joshua Lawrence Chamberlain, a former college professor, was placed at the far left end of the Union line on the rocky slope of Little Round Top. Their brigade commander, Colonel Strong Vincent, told Chamberlain to hold the position at all costs. If it fell, the whole Union flank could be turned.

Confederate regiments, led by the 15th Alabama under Colonel William Oates, attacked up the hill again and again. Chamberlain stretched and bent his line to keep from being outflanked. Casualties mounted, and his men began running out of ammunition.

With another attack coming and no ammunition to stop it, Chamberlain ordered a bayonet charge. The left wing of the regiment swung forward like a door, down the slope into the attackers. The exhausted Confederates broke, and many were captured.

The Union left held. Chamberlain was later awarded the Medal of Honor for his actions that day.
lesson: When you are out of good options, a bold decision made quickly can be safer than waiting. Doing nothing is also a choice.
people: Joshua Lawrence Chamberlain, the 20th Maine, William Oates, Strong Vincent
location: Little Round Top, Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, USA
source: Official reports of the 20th Maine and the 15th Alabama; Chamberlain's later accounts
caveat: Later popular accounts, partly based on Chamberlain's own writings, may overstate the 20th Maine's role, and other officers claimed credit for starting the charge.
